FINANCIAL THINKING / FIELD NOTE

The financial problem comes first. The model can wait.

Nandini Thakur · 3 min read

I like building things. Which makes “let me code it” a very convenient way to avoid admitting I haven’t completely understood the problem yet.

Finance makes that habit especially interesting. There is a model to learn, a dataset to explore, and usually an acronym nearby to make the whole thing feel official. I want the financial intuition underneath all of that.

Start with the decision

The question I’m learning to ask first is: whose decision is this supposed to improve? A researcher looking for a signal, a team assessing risk, and someone reviewing a suspicious transaction are doing different jobs. “Apply AI to finance” is a field of interest. It still needs an actual problem.

For any idea, I want to be able to explain the financial workflow, the information available, the decision being made, and the cost of getting it wrong. Preferably in sentences that don’t require a second glossary.

Then earn the complexity

My learning map moves from financial products and probability towards derivatives, risk, and quantitative research. The purpose is to understand why a method belongs in a problem, what its assumptions buy me, and where those assumptions become inconvenient.

A useful small build should leave me with more than a chart. I want a question, a reproducible method, and an explanation of what I still don’t know. The limitations deserve their own paragraph. They have usually worked quite hard to be there.

The direction I’m taking

I want to stay close to engineering while developing the financial depth to build more useful systems. Eventually, I want to connect the problem, the mathematics, the implementation, and the business judgment. For now, the next step is a smaller question answered properly.

Still thinking this through. A good counterargument is welcome.

YOUR TURN

A question? A better idea?

I have opinions. I’m also quite happy to revise them.
